experiments.scope: The program of proof.md Sections 3 to 5 on the exact sha3-256-r6-prefix-v1 hash with rounds 0 to 5, one absorbed block M(x) (32 little-endian bytes of x, then 103 zero bytes). The 256 walks of the search are advanced together by the bit-sliced register program built by the generator of proof.md Appendix A (executed on Python integers; one integer holds a plane for all trials of the request, trial t in bits 256 t to 256 t + 255, trials never interact). The function iterated is f' = the low 18 bits of the digest of M(x), so the search runs on a 2^18-element function instead of 2^256 (after each step the planes above bit 18 are set to zero, the only difference from the full-size program). Each trial derives its random word from SHAKE-256 of its own seed, follows 256 walks to points whose low 4 bits are zero (walk cap 256 steps), keeps a table end -> (trail number, length), restarts walks at once, and on two trails with the same end replays them with the one-walk program to the first merge. It returns two different messages whose digests agree in the low 18 bits. A mask success is a partial collision of 18 bits, not a collision of the 256-bit digest. Before the trials the program checks the bit-sliced program (256 inputs, two chained steps) and the one-walk program against the plain permutation.
experiments.hypothesis: Every trial returns two different messages whose digests agree on the 18 masked bits (bytes 0 and 1 and the low 2 bits of byte 2), found by walks, a table and the replay and not by a table of all points. The observations are untrusted counters: steps used, trails started, dead walks, attempts, table size, replayed evaluations and executed word operations. Nothing about the cost at 256 bits is inferred from the run.
